validator: draft 1 passes validate.mjs with no problems, soft points or warnings. The faults below are the critic's, not the validator's.
keep: The idea is named up front: lesson 1's ratios need a right angle, and two rules solve the rest.

The cosine rule is derived, not handed over: arm b along the across axis, arm a as lesson 3's turning arm scaled by a, Pythagoras on the gap, and cos² C + sin² C = 1 from lesson 3 collapses it. The minus sign's cause is then the cosine's sign, read off the arm (Cambridge cos 110° slip, brief notes 6.2).
The sine rule is shown by dropping a height (brief: 'shown by dropping a height'), and its formula, which RESEARCH does not quote, is derived on screen rather than cited.
The ambiguous case is lesson 3's two angles with one sine, with the 180° test cited to Bitesize [5]; the swing arm shows none, two and one landing.

Every Cambridge cosine-rule slip in the brief has a DO screen whose wrong answer is that slip: Pythagoras with no right angle (2, 13), the 2 dropped and (a² + b² − 2ab) cos C (4), the minus sign lost and sin for cos (6), the subtraction the wrong way round (8). 'Maths ERROR' is taught as a check from the unit circle (a cosine lies between −1 and 1), since Save My Exams is not in RESEARCH.
Fourteen screens alternate SHOW 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 with DO 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, and close on two mixed puzzles (ships by the cosine rule, a crank by the sine rule where the second angle does not fit).

Every number recomputed: hinge 3 and 4 at 0, 60, 90, 110, 120, 180°; 3-4-6 gives 117.3°; 5-7-8 gives 60°; 6.74 by the sine rule; swing arm sin B = 0.8 and 0.667; ships 73.5; crank 9.2°; worked example 7.68, 44.3°, 85.7°.
fix: Garbled text: screen 14 in whatAmILookingAt reads 'Is the rod's angle to the centre line 9.2°, 9.2° or 170.8°, or no angle at all'. State the three answers plainly: 9.2° only, 9.2° or 170.8°, or no such triangle (each side over the wrong angle, where sin⁻¹ shows an error).
Arithmetic shown from a rounded figure: the worked example writes 140 × 0.643 = 89.99, but 140 × 0.643 is 90.02. Write 140 × cos 50° = 89.99, with the cosine kept unrounded.

False absolute in the sine-rule why: 'drop a line from B square onto side AC' and only A past 90° is handled. If A or C is past 90° the foot lands on AC carried on beyond that corner; say so for both.

Loose wording: 'Two triangles from the same facts are called the ambiguous case.' The ambiguous case is the situation, not the triangles: 'When the same facts fit two triangles, it is called the ambiguous case.'
Vague claim: 'Most triangles have none' is a count no source gives. Say 'Plenty of real triangles have none'.
Shorter than what: 'Close the hinge and the free ends come together, so c is shorter' should say shorter than at 90°, so the comparison with Pythagoras is explicit.

Unreadable risk at 340 px: three bars 'beside' the hinge squeeze both. Put the bars under the hinge, and on screen 3 let the working appear one line at a time with the gap's two dashed sides labelled, so the picture is not crowded with algebra.
verdict: Rewrite as draft 2 with these seven fixes; nothing structural changes.
